audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed penultimate primary stress, secondary two syllables to the left, domain = word after suffixation/compounding) rests on the standard reference grammar (Crowley 1999 PL C-156, sec. 4.3 pp.115-116), which we hold and whose quotation I confirmed verbatim; the earlier sketch (Lynch 1983:149, downloaded now from sealang, independently says 'Stress tends to be penultimate.' Nothing better exists for this moribund language. The only housekeeping points: (a) the record's top-level quote/cite/grade fields are blank while the verified quotation sits in sources/the domain quotation, so the strength of the evidence should be set to primary-reference-grammar-verified; (b) the rule string extrapolates iterative alternating secondaries (101010, 0101010..) whereas Crowley states only one secondary stress on 'the preceding syllable but one' with

sources.quote: "Primary stress in Ura is invariably found on the penultimate syllable. In words of four syllables or more, a secondary stress attaches to the preceding syllable but one." (Crowley 1999:115, §4.3; four-syllable example on p. 116: [ˌsesiˈmaŋsi] 'index finger' = 1010, secondary mark rendered as 'n' by scanned; also [ˈnesi] 'pawpaw' = 10, [niˈmova] 'outrigger pole' = 010. Corroborating: "Stress tends to be penultimate." Lynch 1983:149)
